completed_stage_receipts.summary: Confirmed a cross-owner product-boundary defect: internal executor/readiness modes were surfaced as if they were user-facing routes, obscuring the intended ChatGPT + GitHub Agent product model.
Classified INTERNAL_EXECUTION_ADAPTER_EXPOSED_AS_USER_PRODUCT_ROUTE as CROSS_OWNER_RECURRENT: execution modes are legitimate assurance metadata, but their product boundary was not centrally explicit.

Mapped the parent system as user -> ChatGPT owner/Skill entry -> GitHub engineering/rule authority and owner task state -> capability/readiness dispatch -> internal executor -> one canonical owner workflow -> evidence/artifacts. The four current BUSINESS owners are in scope; business task state and leases are out of scope.

Historical work correctly created first-class guarded chat execution and readiness routing, but never promoted the shared distinction that execution modes are internal dispatch/evidence metadata rather than separate products. Recurrence therefore escalates from owner wording to the shared architecture contract.

First-party OpenAI product architecture supports a Skill as workflow/operating guidance with optional connected tools/MCP. Nothing requires each executor mode to become a separate user workflow or requires MCP for every owner.

Reuse scan found the existing shared architecture contract, readiness contract and validator already own the correct abstraction. No new root policy, registry, permanent Agent, service or MCP layer is needed.

Compared no-change/chat explanation, Financial-only wording, deleting execution-mode identifiers, and a shared product-interface invariant. Accepted the shared invariant because it preserves useful assurance modes while preventing route leakage across owners.

Resolved current BUSINESS topology and owner heads. Normal executor selection is a retrievable system decision, not a user choice; user input is required only for genuine external authorization or business decisions.

Selected existing shared control surfaces: architecture contract owns the product-interface invariant, readiness owns internal dispatch semantics, blueprint explains the product shape, and owner Skill/manifests consume it. No account/custom-instruction change is required.

Designed a compact manifest product_interface contract plus deterministic validation and focused regression. Owner changes are metadata/router wording only; no new business state, mandatory service, startup preload or user-operated mode selector is added.

Payoff/deletion test keeps internal OWNER_NATIVE/CHAT_BRIDGED/DETERMINISTIC_TOOL/ISOLATED_EXTERNAL labels for assurance while removing their user-route semantics. It consolidates rather than adds a parallel workflow or service.
